source.note: Ascribed to the sage Śaunaka (v.8 calls the goddess "dear to Śaunaka"). The only Devanagari witness found (sanskritdocuments.org) is badly garbled, so this text is an edited reconstruction, checked against a second, independent witness: the English-letter romanization on celextel.org (P. R. Ramachander's translation). Emendations, each supported by that second witness, by the anuṣṭubh meter, or by grammar: throughout, सैमं → चेमं (= च इमम्, "and this"; romanized "cha imam"); v.1 एह्यहि → एह्येहि; v.2 प्रगृह्णीधन् → प्रगृह्णीतं (dual imperative, to the two Aśvins), सैमं → चेमां, and स रक्षतां → रक्षतां (the extra स breaks the meter); v.3 रुद्रेशा एकादश → रुद्राश्चैकादश and यक्षागमप्रीतये → युष्माकं प्रीतये (both restore the meter; both as in the romanization); v.4 त्विमाम् → त्विमम् (बलि is masculine, as in every other verse), अस्माकं → युष्माकं and रक्षतु → रक्षत (addressed to the Ādityas, as in the romanization); v.7 प्रभवश्यामः प्रत्यासौ → प्रभवः श्यामः प्रत्यूषो and वसवेष्टौ प्रकीर्तितः → वसवोऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः. The least certain line is v.7's ध्रुवो धुरधरश्चैव (Devanagari ध्रुवाधर धराशैव, romanized "Druvoo dhura dhuraschaiva"), reconstructed so that the verse names exactly eight Vasus; the list is not the usual Purāṇic one. Readings kept where both are words: सापत्यं ("with her child"), बुधश्रेष्ठे (romanization: भूतश्रेष्ठे), निवृत्ते (romanization: निर्वृते).
